claim: The claim that the SV40 found in COVID-19 vaccines is 'the same ingredient' that contaminated the polio vaccine collapses a distinction that the underlying documents keep separate. The polio-era contaminant was whole live Simian Virus 40 — an infectious virus carrying the gene for large T antigen (LT), the viral protein that transforms cells by disabling the p53 and retinoblastoma tumour suppressors. What independent sequencing found in the Pfizer product is the SV40 promoter-enhancer, a short piece of regulatory DNA that switches gene expression on, carried over in residual plasmid from manufacturing. It is not the virus and does not itself encode LT; responding to Florida's surgeon general in December 2023, the FDA stated that 'No SV40 proteins are encoded for or are present in the vaccines.' That distinction is real, but it does not make the sequence self-evidently inert, and the reassuring framing overstates the case in the other direction. In peer-reviewed work published in Tumour Virus Research in 2024, Šenigl, Alinikula and colleagues report that the SV40 enhancer is itself a potent target for somatic hypermutation, concluding that 'the ability of the SV40 enhancer to target somatic hypermutation to LT is a potential source of LT truncation events that could contribute to tumorigenesis in various cell types, thereby linking SV40 infection with malignant development through a novel mutagenic pathway.' That study examines the enhancer alongside the viral LT gene in cell culture; it is not a study of vaccines and does not measure any effect in vaccinated people. A related sub-claim — that the SV40 sequences sit upstream of an oncogene — is contradicted by the annotated sequence of the product itself. GenBank PP544446, a 7,692-base-pair deposit of the BNT162b2 vaccine plasmid, places the SV40 enhancer at bases 1040-1185 and the next gene downstream, at 1392-2186, is neoR/kanR, the kanamycin-neomycin antibiotic-resistance marker used to select the plasmid in bacteria. The only other protein-coding sequence in the entire plasmid is the spike gene at 3578-7399, which runs off its own separate promoter. There is no oncogene in the construct. Health Canada, which examined Pfizer's own filing, stated that 'the presence of the SV40 promoter enhancer sequence is not the same as the presence of the whole virus itself,' that the fragment 'is inactive, has no functional role,' and that 'any claims that the presence of the SV40 promoter enhancer sequence is linked to an increased risk of cancer are unfounded' — while also confirming that 'although the full DNA sequence of the Pfizer plasmid was provided at the time of initial filing, the sponsor did not specifically identify the SV40 sequence,' and that it 'expects sponsors to identify any biologically functional DNA sequences within a plasmid (such as an SV40 enhancer) at the time of submission.' No study has demonstrated integration of vaccine residual DNA into the genome of a vaccinated person. What is documented is presence and non-disclosure; what is asserted on top of it — that the sequence causes cancer, or that it is the polio contaminant returning — is not established by the sequencing work.

notes: Written to hold the line in both directions, which is the whole point of this record. Against the reel: 'the same ingredient' is wrong as stated — live oncogenic virus in 1955-63 versus a regulatory DNA element in 2021, and the FDA's 'no SV40 proteins' statement is on the record. Against the standard rebuttal: 'it's just a promoter, promoters are inert' is also not established — the Šenigl/Alinikula group published a peer-reviewed mechanism by which the enhancer sequence itself has tumorigenic potential, and that paper is in a virology journal, not an advocacy outlet. Its limits are stated in the claim so it is not oversold: cell culture, studied with the LT gene present, not a vaccine study. Follows the model of [[2021-graphene-oxide-vaccine-claim-001]] for status. The presence/non-disclosure facts live in [[2025-residual-dna-001]] and are not restated here. The historical predicate is [[1961-sv40-polio-001]]. RESOLVED 2026-08-01: the 'sits above an oncogene' sub-claim was checked against the deposited plasmid and is false as to this construct. GenBank PP544446 has exactly two coding sequences across 7,692 bp — neoR/kanR (1392..2186) and the spike gene (3578..7399) — and the SV40 enhancer at 1040..1185 sits immediately upstream of the antibiotic-resistance marker, which is the canonical pcDNA3.1 arrangement. Provenance caveat worth keeping in mind: PP544446 was deposited by D. Raoult (IHU Mediterranee Infection, Marseille) from Illumina sequencing of a vaccine batch, i.e. a third-party read of the product, not Pfizer's own regulatory filing. It is nonetheless a public annotated sequence of the actual product and no competing annotation places an oncogene in the plasmid. Health Canada's wording is now quoted on both sides: it rejects the cancer linkage AND confirms Pfizer did not specifically identify the SV40 element in its filing.
